item.title: jscrambler npm Infostealer Compromise and Global CMS Exploitation Campaign
item.content:encoded:
Australia warns of global campaign targeting vulnerable CMS platforms — Must Read

Australia’s Cyber Security Centre warned that attackers are globally scanning and exploiting vulnerable CMS platforms and plugins, including WordPress, Craft CMS, Joomla JCE, and others, to deploy webshells on compromised sites. Website admins should urgently patch CMS software, themes, and plugins, remove unused components, and monitor for unauthorized files or suspicious server processes.

  • The Australian Cyber Security Centre issued an alert about a global exploitation campaign targeting vulnerable content management systems and plugins.
  • The ACSC said many small- to medium-sized Australian businesses have been impacted, with webshells being deployed on their sites.
  • The campaign targets vulnerabilities in CMS platforms and plugins including WordPress, Craft CMS, MaxSite CMS, MetInfo CMS, and Joomla JCE.
  • The ACSC noted that the campaign might be supported by AI, which can help threat actors accelerate attacks and scale exploitation of emerging flaws.
  • Website administrators are advised to apply the latest security updates, remove unused components, enable automatic updates where possible, and monitor for unauthorized file creation.

jscrambler npm Package Compromised in Supply Chain Attack — Must Read

The npm package jscrambler@8.14.0 was compromised with a preinstall hook that silently drops and runs platform-specific native infostealer binaries during installation. Anyone who installed it should remove the version, revert to a clean release, and rotate credentials exposed on affected developer or CI systems.

  • The compromised jscrambler@8.14.0 npm release, published on July 11, 2026, added an undocumented preinstall hook that invokes dist/setup.js during npm install.
  • Version 8.14.0 introduced new install-time files and hidden platform-specific binaries for Linux, macOS, and Windows that were absent from jscrambler@8.13.0.
  • The loader reads an obfuscated CSI container, selects a binary based on the operating system, decompresses it to a hidden temporary file, marks it executable, and launches it in the background.
  • The embedded Rust-built payloads are described as cross-platform infostealers targeting developer-focused secrets including cryptocurrency wallets, AI coding assistant configs, cloud credentials, messaging apps, browsers, gaming sessions, and OS keyrings.
  • Users are advised to remove jscrambler@8.14.0, rotate credentials accessible to affected development or CI environments, review installation logs for dist/setup.js execution, and pin to jscrambler@8.13.0 or another verified clean release.
